subject: turtle
reasoning:
I'm planning out a TypeScript module for building a stylized sea turtle with the SDK, thinking through realistic proportions (around 1.1-1.2m shell length like a green sea turtle) and setting up the basic skeleton structure starting with the root node.

Now I'm working through the joint hierarchy: a hips/body root, a neck-head-jaw chain, shoulder and hip joints for four flippers with the hind pair smaller and set further back, a short tail chain, and eye placements. For the shell itself, I'm considering a loft approach instead of a simple lathe, since a lathe would produce a circular dome while a loft lets me define elongated stations with varying width and height along the body axis to get the elliptical carapace shape I want.

I'm thinking the shell should be a flattened dome—wider and longer than it is tall—so I'll keep the loft's height profile shallow while the plastron covers the underside with a cream countershade. For texture, I plan to use a scale-pattern paint across olive and brown tones to define scute outlines on the carapace, with a darker marginal rim, while the head and skin get a green-grey base with cream countershading underneath.

For dimensions I'm working in meters: shell spans roughly z=-0.45 to 0.45, head extends out to about z=0.75, giving a total length near 1.1m, which matches a sea turtle's scale. I'm placing the shell centered around y=0.26 with the bottom near y=0.12, and working out flipper joint positions (shoulder, elbow, wrist, tip) so the front flippers extend sideways and slightly down—leaving them hovering just above the ground rather than touching, which should still satisfy the resting-pose floor rule.

Since the lowest points need to nearly touch y=0, I'm lowering the whole turtle: shell bottom around y=0.04, belly plastron just above that, and flipper tips sinking close to y=0. I'm figuring out how to shape the flippers as flattened paddles—considering a tapered tube sweep with an elliptical cross-section to get that flat fin look rather than a round limb.

Working through the orientation math for the flipper paddle's extrusion directions...

I'm planning the flipper as a joint-attached extruded paddle shape rigged to a wrist bone, with a chain of shoulder/elbow/wrist/tip joints for rigging, and mirroring the sideways orientation symmetrically for left and right. Now I'm sketching the outline points for the leaf-shaped paddle profile.

Working out the flipper joint coordinates...

I need to lower the shell so it barely touches the floor rather than sinking too far in — adjusting the bottom to around y=0.01 instead of 0.04. I'm sketching the carapace loft stations front-to-back, varying width and height to get a rounded, flattened sea turtle profile, making sure the lowest point of the midsection lands near the ground plane.

Rechecking the loft convention, I realize width/height values should represent full dimensions rather than half-widths, so I'm redoing the stations with doubled values and centering y at 0.17 so the belly still clears the floor by about 0.02. I'm also considering whether to bind the loft to the hips joint as a rigid bone and whether the default octagonal cross-section (8 sides) will look too faceted, wondering if I should bump up the sides for a smoother shell.

For shell texture, I'm planning to layer a scales pattern using a few olive/brown base tones with a darker edge color, sized around 0.09 with thin borders, then apply a countershade so the top stays darker and the underside fades toward cream — mimicking a sea turtle's lighter plastron. I'm deciding the skin tone for the head and flippers should follow a similar olive-grey to cream countershade gradient.

Now I'm laying out the neck as a joint chain of four points curving upward from the body toward the head tip, naming the middle segments "neck1" through "neck3" with the final point becoming the "head" joint, oriented along the neck's tangent direction so the head naturally angles forward.

For the actual geometry, I'm sweeping a tapered tube along the neck chain for the skin, then considering a scaled sphere positioned and oriented relative to the head joint's local frame to form the turtle's rounded skull shape.

For the beak, I'm planning a jaw joint offset forward and slightly down from the head, with upper and lower beak pieces built as tapered capsules anchored to the head and jaw bones respectively, colored separately for the beak material.

For eyes, I'm placing small dark spheres on either side of the head using mirrored left/right offsets, positioning them just at the head's surface so they sit embedded naturally into the scaled head sphere.

I'm now designing the full rig: a hips root joint, a neck chain with named segments leading to a head joint, front flipper chains (shoulder-elbow-wrist-hand) with flattened paddle extrusions attached rigidly to the hand, smaller hind flipper chains with their own paddles, and a short tail chain, all sized so the lowest point stays the shell bottom for proper grounding.

I'm settling on a color palette using scattered shell tones with a dark edge, a countershaded skin gradient from olive-green to pale cream, dark eyes, and a brownish beak color.

Writing TypeScript build code...

I'm sketching the head details -- a sphere for the skull, a jaw joint aimed slightly down and forward, upper and lower beak capsules, and symmetric eye placement using surface-nearest hits on the head sphere so the eyes sit correctly on the curved surface.

Still writing component code...

I'm finishing the limb and tail construction -- mirrored front and hind flipper chains with paddle extrusions sized and offset along each limb's local axis, plus a short tapering tail chain -- then wrapping it all up by returning the root and exporting the build function, making sure only the imports I actually use (THREE, createBuilder, catmull, countershade, scales) are included.
